title: 1 Samuel 30
paragraphs: ¹ On the third day, when David and his men reached Ziklag, they found that the Amalekites had raided the Negev and attacked Ziklag. They had burned it to the ground ² and taken captive the women and everyone else there — young and old alike. They had not killed anyone, but had taken them all and moved on. ³ When David and his men arrived at the city, they found it burned down, and their wives, sons, and daughters had been taken captive. ⁴ David and his men wept aloud until they had no more strength to weep. ⁵ Both of David's wives had been taken captive — Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail, the widow of Nabal of Carmel.

⁶ David was in a desperate situation, because the men were talking about stoning him — each man was bitter over the loss of his sons and daughters. But David found strength in the LORD his God. ⁷ He said to Abiathar the priest, son of Ahimelech, "Bring me the ephod." Abiathar brought it, ⁸ and David inquired of the LORD, "Should I pursue this raiding party? Will I overtake them?" The LORD answered, "Pursue them. You will certainly overtake them and rescue everyone." ⁹ David set out with his six hundred men and reached the Besor Ravine, where some of them stayed behind. ¹⁰ David and four hundred men continued the pursuit, but two hundred were too exhausted to cross the ravine and remained there.

¹¹ They came across an Egyptian in the open country and brought him to David. They gave him food to eat and water to drink, ¹² and also gave him a piece of pressed fig cake and two clusters of raisins. After eating, his strength came back to him — he had gone three days and three nights without food or water. ¹³ David asked him, "Who do you belong to? Where are you from?" He said, "I'm an Egyptian — a servant of an Amalekite. My master abandoned me when I fell ill three days ago. ¹⁴ We raided the Negev of the Cherethites, part of Judah's territory, and the Negev of Caleb. We burned Ziklag." ¹⁵ David asked, "Can you lead me to this raiding party?" He answered, "Swear to me by God that you won't kill me or hand me back to my master, and I'll take you to them."

¹⁶ He led David to them, and they found the Amalekites spread out across the countryside, eating, drinking, and celebrating over all the plunder they had taken from the land of the Philistines and from Judah. ¹⁷ David fought them from dusk until the evening of the next day. Not one of them escaped except four hundred young men who rode off on camels and fled. ¹⁸ David recovered everything the Amalekites had taken, including his two wives. ¹⁹ Nothing was missing — young or old, sons or daughters, plunder or anything else they had taken. David brought it all back. ²⁰ He also took all the flocks and herds, which were driven ahead of the other livestock, and the men said, "This is David's plunder."

²¹ Then David returned to the two hundred men who had been too exhausted to follow him and had stayed at the Besor Ravine. They came out to meet David and his men. When David approached, he greeted them warmly. ²² But some troublemakers among David's men spoke up: "These men didn't go with us, so we're not giving them any of the plunder we recovered. Each man can take his wife and children and go." ²³ But David said, "No, my brothers — don't do that with what the LORD has given us. He has kept us safe and handed over the forces that attacked us. ²⁴ Who would ever agree to what you're saying? The share of the man who stays with the supplies is the same as the share of the man who goes into battle. They will share alike." ²⁵ And from that day forward, David made it a standing rule and regulation for Israel, which remains to this day.

²⁶ When David arrived at Ziklag, he sent portions of the plunder to the elders of Judah — his friends — saying, "Here is a gift for you from the plunder of the LORD's enemies." ²⁷ He sent gifts to those in Bethel, Ramoth Negev, and Jattir; ²⁸ to those in Aroer, Siphmoth, and Eshtemoa; ²⁹ to those in Racal, the towns of the Jerahmeelites, and the towns of the Kenites; ³⁰ to those in Hormah, Bor-ashan, and Athach;
³¹ and to those in Hebron — to all the places where David and his men had roamed.
